title: Gusseted thumb fingerless mitts
subtitle: Seamless fingerless mitts with a classic thumb gusset for a better-fitting thumb opening.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in DK wool with a thumb gusset for a close, comfortable fit at the base of the thumb. Worked in the round in stocking stitch. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: The thumb gusset is the standard construction in classic British and Scandinavian mitten patterns from the early 20th century, documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), Weldon's Practical Knitter (various series), and the Harmony Guide series. The construction is cross-referenced across 5 or more published sources.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening shaped by increasing a wedge of stitches over several rounds at the thumb position, then placing them on waste yarn. The wedge gives a better anatomical fit at the base of the thumb than a simple hole.
An increase worked by lifting the horizontal strand between two stitches with the left needle and knitting into the back of it. M1L lifts from left to right; M1R lifts from right to left.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts in DK wool, worked in the round in stocking stitch, with a
gusseted thumb
for a close, comfortable fit at the base of the thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The gusset is built by increasing two stitches every three rounds to form a small wedge. The wedge stitches are placed on waste yarn when they reach full thumb width, and the hand continues over the gap. After the hand is bound off, the gusset stitches are returned to the needle and worked as the thumb tube. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 85 g (185 m / 200 yards) of DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 85 g (about 185 m / 200 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the gusset, 1 for palm midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the gusset

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
Stitches used
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 22 (24, 26) rounds of 2x2 rib.
Hand and gusset
Switch to stocking stitch. Work 4 rounds. Place gusset markers around the first 2 stitches of the round.
Increase round: SM,
M1R
, k2, M1L, SM, knit to end. Work 2 plain rounds. Repeat the increase round every 3rd round until the gusset holds 14 (16, 18) stitches. About 6 increase rounds are needed.
Place gusset on waste yarn
On the next round: slip the 14 (16, 18) gusset stitches to waste yarn. Cast on 2 stitches over the gap using backward-loop cast-on. Continue in stocking stitch for 20 (22, 24) rounds. Bind off.
Thumb

Return gusset stitches to needle. Pick up 2 stitches from the bridging cast-on. Total: 16 (18, 20) thumb stitches. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds of stocking stitch. Work 4 rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults
Hole at the bridge between gusset and hand: the 2 bridging cast-on stitches were skipped. Pick up 2 stitches from the cast-on when working the thumb, not just the gusset stitches.

Gusset increases lean the wrong way: M1R and M1L were swapped. M1R leans right (for the left edge of the gusset) and M1L leans left (for the right edge). Always work M1R before the gusset stitches and M1L after.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Close any small holes at the gusset corners with your tapestry needle.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

The same gusset construction scales to full mittens by extending the hand section upward and shaping the tip with decreases. The gusseted cabled fingerless mitts add a cable panel on the back once the gusset is secure.
